text:
mike: Getting a support ticket from a new user running the .NET quickstart. They say the sample app deadlocks after a few minutes and then they get a flood of 429s.
anya: Do we have a repro? Which SDK version?
mike: They used dotnet-sdk v0.9.1 (our public quickstart references that). Behavior: start five paginated workers, after ~90s everything stalls. Logs show AcquireAsync never returns for some goroutine-ish thread (Task) and inflight counter is stuck.
leo: Interesting 0% different language but same class of bug: token bucket + retry/backoff holding slots. .NET had an internal SemaphoreSlim wrapper that didn't release when auth refresh threw an exception during retry.
anya: Can you paste the code pattern in the quickstart?
mike: It's the naive pattern many users use:
```csharp
foreach (var page in client.Paginate(query)) {
  // fire-and-forget processing
  _ = Task.Run(async () => await ProcessPage(page));
}
```
No awaits, no bounding, and the SDK's AcquireAsync is internal to the paginator so users don't see it.
leo: Oof. Because AcquireAsync is internal, users don't have an obvious place to call Release(). That means SDK must be defensive: ensure Acquire/Release paired even when user code drops tasks.
anya: Proposed fixes: 1) quickstart change to show a bounded concurrency pattern with a public limiter helper for .NET, 2) make .NET SDK ensure semaphore slot is released on any auth/retry failure path and make Release idempotent, 3) add a server-side metric and client telemetry for "lease-age" to detect long-held slots.
mike: Also, add a recommended pattern for .NET using Channel<T> and a bounded worker pool so users don't copy naive fire-and-forget loops. Example:```csharp
var channel = Channel.CreateBounded<Page>(new BoundedChannelOptions(16) { SingleReader = false });
// producer: write to channel
// consumer tasks: read from channel and ProcessPage with try/finally Release
```
leo: Parity note: Python/Go/JS have opt-in limiter helpers but .NET didn't. Let's add a public BackpressureLimiter API that mirrors signatures of other SDKs. Defaults: MaxConcurrent=8, SmoothingMs=2500.
anya: Tests: (A) unit test simulating auth refresh failures mid-work and assert that activeSlots returns to zero after retries, (B) stress test running 200 concurrent paginators to ensure inflight <= max + 1.
ci-bot: CI: branch `dotnet/backpressure` created, integration tests queued.
mike: Short-term mitigations: update quickstart to use explicit bounded Channel example, push a hotfix sample. Longer-term: SDK patch to add limiter and safe retry accounting.
leo: I'll take the SDK patch. Make Release idempotent and ensure AcquireAsync registers a CancellationToken that cleans up slot on cancellation or auth failure. Add finalizer guard (weakref) to release if GCed after TTL as a last resort.
anya: Docs: add a migration note and a bold warning at the top of quickstart about copy/pasting naive loops. We'll also add a "Common gotchas" section referencing JS/Python examples.
ci-bot: CI: `dotnet/backpressure` tests started.
mike: Once CI passes, cut a sample-app hotfix and tag onboarding channel with the updated quickstart. This should reduce early support tickets from .NET users.
leo: I'll also coordinate parity sync so Go/TS/Py/NET all land helper APIs in the same sprint.
anya: Thanks team. I'll file DOC-330 for the docs change and SDK-985 for the SDK PR.
ci-bot: CI: integration flaky (2/15) f6; will report back.
mike: Great work. Hopefully this prevents more confusing early experiences. :pray:
